newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil falls again.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil falls again.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil was weaker again on Friday as more product piled up and buyers held back, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $89 and $90 fob ARA and bunker demand was described as adequate.
High sulphur barges were weaker. An ARA player sold a cargo to a trader, for lifting any time in March, at $92 cif NWE.
Another ARA player was heard to be offering Scandinavian material at around $94 cif NWE.
Low sulphur fuel oil was weaker again.

Two potential buyers - one in Italy for a 25,000 tonne requirement in early March, and one in southern France, were still seen on the horizon. This material was under discussion on a quotes-related basis, traders said.
But supply remains long in northwest Europe and dealers said physical cargo prices had slipped in line with crude oil futures to around $95/$97 fob NWE.
